title: Fethiye to Kaş & Kalkan: Driving the D400 Coastal Highway

metaDescription: Drive Fethiye to Kaş and Kalkan on the D400 with realistic times, Saklıkent, Patara, and Kaputaş stops, dolmuş luggage tips, and safe pull-outs.
quickAnswer: Driving from Fethiye to Kalkan takes 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 25 minutes (80 km), and continuing along the cliffside D400 to Kaş takes 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours total (107 km). Private transfers comfortably fit stops at Saklıkent Gorge or Patara, whereas public dolmuş minibuses struggle with large suitcases.

body.text: How long is the drive from Fethiye to Kalkan and Kaş?

Without stops, the direct drive from central Fethiye to Kalkan takes 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 25 minutes along the inland D400 through Eşen and Kınık. Reaching Kaş adds another 25 to 30 minutes along the dramatic two-lane coastal cliff road past Kaputaş Beach, bringing the Fethiye-to-Kaş total to 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours.

Expect slower progress between late June and early September, when tour coaches, rental cars, and roadside parking near Kaputaş Beach narrow the Kalkan–Kaş stretch to a crawl. Leaving from Ölüdeniz or Kayaköy adds 20 to 30 minutes at the start of the trip. Drivers can check seasonal resurfacing or rockfall advisories on the [General Directorate of Highways (KGM) route portal](https://yol.kgm.gov.tr/guzergahanalizi) before setting out.
Which stops (Saklıkent, Patara, Kaputaş Beach) fit into a transfer day?

You can comfortably fit one major stop—either Saklıkent Gorge or Patara—plus a quick coastal viewpoint pause near Kaputaş Beach into a single transfer day. Attempting all three between hotel check-out in Fethiye and check-in in Kaş usually feels rushed, especially in peak afternoon heat when parking near Kaputaş fills completely.
Plan each stop around its distance off the D400:

items: Saklıkent Gorge: A 20-minute detour inland from the Karaçay junction. Allow 90 minutes to walk the shaded canyon floor and rinse off before getting back into your transfer vehicle. Bring water shoes and a dry change of clothes in a daypack.

Patara Ancient City & Beach: Turns off the D400 near Ovaköy (about 15 minutes before Kalkan). The [Patara Archaeological Site](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=PTR01&DistId=PTR) features the restored Lycian League parliament building and theater, followed by an 18-kilometer sand beach. Budget 2 hours minimum.

Kaputaş Beach: Sits directly beneath the D400 bridge 7 km east of Kalkan. Between 10:30 and 16:30 in summer, roadside parking is chaotic; it works best as a quick morning swim or brief stop only when your driver can wait safely away from the blind curves.

body.text: Are intercity dolmuş minibuses practical with large suitcases?

Intercity dolmuş minibuses between Fethiye Otogar, Kalkan, and Kaş are cheap and frequent, running roughly every 30 to 60 minutes in season, but they are poorly suited to travelers with large hard-shell suitcases. Most vehicles on the Fethiye–Kaş line are 16-to-20-seat minibuses with shallow rear boots that fill quickly with local parcels and backpacks.

During busy summer departures, drivers often place oversized luggage in the center aisle or ask passengers to pay for an extra seat if bags block access. Furthermore, Fethiye Otogar sits inland from the harbor, and Kalkan's bus station sits at the top of a steep hill above the old town. If you are carrying more than one cabin-sized bag per person—or traveling with children—a pre-booked private van or rental car saves considerable friction.
Where are the safest pull-outs for coastal photos?

Never stop on the narrow shoulder along the cliffside bends immediately west or east of Kaputaş Beach, where oncoming drivers have limited sightlines. Instead, use designated paved lay-bys with clear visibility in both directions, notably the panoramic terrace overlooking Kalkan Bay just above town and the wide gravel turnouts along the approach toward Kaş Peninsula.
Follow this D400 transfer safety checklist:

items: Use marked lay-bys only: Pull completely off the white shoulder line on straight sections where approaching trucks can see you from at least 150 meters away.
Avoid the Kaputaş cliff curves at midday: Park only in officially marked roadside bays or walk down from the designated municipal parking zone if spaces are open.
Time the sunset glare: Driving eastbound toward Kaş in the morning is easy on the eyes, while late-afternoon westbound drivers face low sun directly on the bends above Kalkan.
Keep valuables out of sight at stops: If stopping at Patara or Saklıkent with a rental car, keep luggage completely concealed in the trunk or hire a private driver who stays with the vehicle.

faq.q: Is the D400 highway between Fethiye and Kaş safe to drive yourself?
faq.a: Yes. The road is fully paved, well-signposted, and routinely driven by rental cars. The inland Fethiye–Kalkan stretch is broad and straightforward; only the final 27 km from Kalkan to Kaş requires slower, attentive driving around coastal curves.

faq.q: Can you visit both Saklıkent and Patara on the way from Fethiye to Kaş?
faq.a: Yes, if you leave Fethiye by 08:30 with a private driver or rental car. Spend 90 minutes at Saklıkent in the cooler morning, have lunch near Patara or Kalkan, visit Patara in the early afternoon, and reach Kaş by 17:00.

faq.q: How much does a dolmuş from Fethiye to Kaş take?
faq.a: The direct Fethiye–Kaş minibus typically takes 2 hours 15 minutes to 2 hours 30 minutes because it makes brief passenger stops in Kemer (Seydikemer), Eşen, Kınık, and Kalkan Otogar.

faq.q: Where is the nearest airport to Fethiye and Kaş?
faq.a: [Dalaman Airport (DLM)](https://dhmi.gov.tr/Sayfalar/Havalimani/Dalaman/AnaSayfa.aspx) is 50 minutes from Fethiye and roughly 2 hours to 2 hours 15 minutes from Kaş, making it the closest airport for both towns.

faq.q: Do you need a MuseumPass for Patara Archaeological Site?
faq.a: Foreign visitors can buy a single entry ticket at the Patara gate or online through the [Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism e-ticket portal](https://muze.gov.tr/ETicket). The ticket covers access to both the archaeological ruins and the beach road.

faq.q: Is parking easy in Kaş town center if I rent a car?
faq.a: Street parking inside central Kaş is very tight from May through October. Book a hotel with dedicated parking or use the municipal paid parking lots near the marina and bus station.
